title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #3 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which force pulls objects down towards the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. Wind
   B. Friction
   C. Sound
   D. Gravity

2. Which of these holds objects together? (1 mark)
   A. A smooth floor
   B. A rolling ball
   C. Oil
   D. Glue

3. What happens when you push a book gently with a finger compared with a hard push? (1 mark)
   A. It moves slowly with the gentle push
   B. It flies away with the gentle push
   C. It does not move with the hard push
   D. It moves faster with the gentle push

4. Which of these shows that friction produces heat? (1 mark)
   A. Rubbing hands together
   B. Pouring water
   C. Looking at a torch
   D. Drawing with chalk

5. A stone and a crumpled paper are dropped together. They land almost together because (1 mark)
   A. Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   B. There is no gravity
   C. The paper is heavier
   D. The stone is lighter

6. A ball is rolling and you kick it in the direction it moves. What happens? (1 mark)
   A. It stops
   B. It speeds up
   C. It changes into a solid
   D. It gets smaller

7. Which surface gives the most friction? (1 mark)
   A. A rough carpet
   B. A smooth ice surface
   C. A polished tile
   D. An oiled floor

8. Where are ball bearings found? (1 mark)
   A. In bicycle wheels
   B. In a book
   C. In a pencil
   D. In a cup

9. Why do people spread ash or sand on a slippery path? (1 mark)
   A. To reduce friction
   B. To make it hot
   C. To make it heavy
   D. To increase friction

10. Why is it better to use daylight than electric light in the day? (1 mark)
   A. It saves money
   B. It costs more
   C. It is unsafe
   D. It makes rooms dark

11. Which of these gives artificial light by burning paraffin? (1 mark)
   A. Star
   B. Lightning
   C. Sun
   D. Paraffin lamp

12. Why do houses have windows? (1 mark)
   A. To let in daylight
   B. To make noise
   C. To keep out light
   D. To let in only rain

13. Why do some farmers use bright lights near animal pens at night? (1 mark)
   A. To warm animals
   B. To make animals heavier
   C. To make animals sleepy
   D. To scare away wild animals

14. A lighthouse is used to (1 mark)
   A. Cook food
   B. Warn ships of danger
   C. Dry clothes
   D. Grow plants

15. Which of these uses heat to change dough into bread? (1 mark)
   A. Baking
   B. Washing
   C. Freezing
   D. Cutting

16. Which of these helps to prevent burns? (1 mark)
   A. Holding hot handles
   B. Touching hot pots
   C. Playing near fire
   D. Using gloves

17. Why does hot tea cool down? (1 mark)
   A. It gains cold
   B. It loses heat to the air and cup
   C. It gains light
   D. It becomes heavier

18. In the water cycle, what does heat from the sun do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes water heavy
   B. Removes all water
   C. Freezes water
   D. Turns water into vapour

19. Why does an ice cube melt in your hand? (1 mark)
   A. The ice makes heat
   B. Cold goes into your hand
   C. The hand makes water
   D. Heat goes from your hand into the ice

20. Which of these is NOT a source of heat? (1 mark)
   A. The sun
   B. A kettle
   C. A burning log
   D. A cold stone in the shade

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Discuss how a family can light their home cheaply and safely. (5 marks)

22. Explain how wet clothes dry in the sun. (3 marks)

23. Why should you not touch a hot object to find out how hot it is? What should you use? (3 marks)

24. Explain what gravity is and give two examples of its effects. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to make a pair of kitchen gloves from local materials. (4 marks)

26. Give two effects of force on objects. (2 marks)

27. Name two ways of lighting a house during the day. (2 marks)

28. Give three examples where a force holds objects together. (3 marks)

29. State two uses of light. (2 marks)

30. Explain why heat from the sun is important to the Earth. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #3 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Gravity
   Gravity pulls things towards the centre of the Earth.

2. D — Glue
   Glue, nails and ropes use forces to hold things together.

3. A — It moves slowly with the gentle push
   A bigger force gives a bigger effect.

4. A — Rubbing hands together
   Rubbing surfaces produces heat.

5. A — Gravity pulls both and air pushes little on the crumpled paper
   The air has very little effect on the crumpled paper.

6. B — It speeds up
   A force in the direction of movement increases speed.

7. A — A rough carpet
   Rough surfaces give more friction.

8. A — In bicycle wheels
   Bicycle wheels use ball bearings.

9. D — To increase friction
   Rough material improves grip.

10. A — It saves money
   Sunlight is free.

11. D — Paraffin lamp
   A paraffin lamp is a made light source.

12. A — To let in daylight
   Windows allow sunlight to enter the room.

13. D — To scare away wild animals
   Bright lights can scare away predators.

14. B — Warn ships of danger
   Lighthouses show ships where land or rocks are.

15. A — Baking
   Baking uses heat.

16. D — Using gloves
   Gloves give protection.

17. B — It loses heat to the air and cup
   Heat goes from the tea to the cooler surroundings.

18. D — Turns water into vapour
   Heat causes evaporation from seas and rivers.

19. D — Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   Heat moves from the warm hand to the ice.

20. D — A cold stone in the shade
   A cold stone gives out no heat of its own.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use windows and translucent sheets by day, solar lamps and LED bulbs at night, keep candles and paraffin away from cloth, turn off lights when not needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Heat from the sun makes the water evaporate. It changes to vapour and goes into the air so the clothes become dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sun heat, 1 mark for evaporation, 1 mark for the result.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can burn your skin. Use a thermometer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for burns, 1 mark for using a thermometer, 1 mark for reason it is safe.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth. It makes rain fall and makes a thrown ball come down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each example.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose thick cotton cloth or old towel. Trace and cut two mitten shapes. Add an inner layer. Sew them together leaving the wrist open. Turn it inside out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: Change shape, start motion, stop motion, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction, hold things together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Windows and translucent roof sheets (skylights).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Glue holding paper, nails holding wood, rope tying things, stitches holding cloth, screws.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: To see, for safety, to discourage pests, for plants to make food, to dry clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: It warms the Earth so plants and animals can live, it dries things, and helps the water cycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.
